key_insight: SAGE-PINN eliminates the cylindrical-axis singularity in axisymmetric PINNs by reparameterizing the geometry and embedding conservation and boundary conditions directly into the network.
engineering_relevance: It enables mesh-free simulation of coupled flow and heat transfer in cylindrical multiphysics systems such as stenosed arteries, with improved stability across varied flow regimes.
method: Uses parity-preserving variable s = r^2 and a modified stream-function form to remove explicit 1/r singular terms.
Enforces boundary conditions exactly with analytical boundary-fitted ansätze.
Stabilizes training with staged momentum-thermal-joint optimization, residual normalization, continuation in Péclet/Richardson numbers, and a physics-scaled drift guard.
evidence_signal: Validated against finite-element reference solutions without labeled data; mass conservation stays at single-precision round-off, with reported central-range errors of 1.6% for axial velocity and 9.1% for temperature.
watch_item: Performance degrades in extreme regimes, especially strongly buoyancy-influenced slow flow and highly advection-dominated heat transfer.
paper_title: SAGE-PINN: A Singularity-free Axisymmetric Geometry-Encoded Physics-Informed Neural Network for Axisymmetric Multiphysics Flow in Cylindrical Coordinates
